A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VideoTree research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables, equations, and algorithms, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original VideoTree evaluations on EgoSchema, NExT-QA, and IntentQA, together with quantitative ablations and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and reports additional Video-MME evaluations, model comparisons, timing measurements, ablations, and a failure case.

M1.justification: The core clustering, relevance-guided tree expansion, and caption-based reasoning procedure remains, and the main prompts are unchanged. However, v2 adds an inference variant using open-source reasoners and selecting answers through option log-likelihood scores rather than generation (Section 5.2.2, Table 4).

E1.justification: v2 adds Video-MME's long split, containing 30–60-minute videos averaging 44 minutes. This substantially extends evaluated video duration beyond v1's seconds-to-minutes benchmarks. EgoSchema, NExT-QA, and IntentQA remain; IntentQA moves to Appendix B.2.

E2.justification: Comparators on retained benchmarks expand to include LangRepo, LVNet, LifelongMemory, Video-LLaVA+INTP, and additional video LLMs. IntentQA gains VGT, Vamos, and LangRepo comparisons. LongViViT, MC-ViT-L, and InternVideo2 results disappear, while SeViLA remains only in the IntentQA comparison. Figure 3 also adds VideoAgent to the caption-budget comparison.

E3.justification: v2 introduces log-likelihood evaluation with Mistral-7B and Mixtral-8×7B, smaller visual-encoder configurations, shared-captioner controls, stage-level timing, and Video-MME sampling at 0.125 FPS. Accuracy and the 500-question EgoSchema ablation set remain unchanged. The newly stated 1 FPS sampling for retained benchmarks is additional disclosure, not evidence of changed preprocessing.

E4.justification: v2 adds timing and LLM-call analyses, visual-encoder scaling, relevance-count threshold sensitivity, shared-captioner evaluation, and a washing-dishes failure case. Component-removal tests revise the investigation of adaptivity and hierarchy. The explicit static-tree comparison, full maximum-depth sweep, and BLIP-2/LaViLa factorial ablation disappear; branch-width and maximum-breadth analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 Table 7 reports empirical error bars, including EgoSchema subset 66.2±1.2, NExT-QA average 73.5±0.4, and IntentQA 66.9±0.6. v2 removes this uncertainty analysis without replacement. Neither version specifies run counts or explains how the error bars were calculated.

E6.justification: Table 1's reported NExT-QA average changes from 73.5 to 75.6, with all three question-type scores revised. EgoSchema 66.2/61.1 and IntentQA 66.9 remain. v2 adds Video-MME accuracy of 54.2, open-source-reasoner results, and timing measurements; caption counts and breadth-ablation values also change. Conflicting validation/test wording in v2 prevents confidently treating the NExT-QA revision as an identical-setting gain.

T1.justification: The clustering formulation in Equation 1 and underlying mathematical definitions remain equivalent. Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs. The rewritten algorithm and three-level relevance explanation do not introduce a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a training-free, query-adaptive hierarchical representation that improves reasoning accuracy and efficiency. v2 updates headline comparisons, adds explicit claims about very long videos and open-source reasoners, and replaces v1's fixed improvement margins and 40% inference-time claim with revised benchmark and efficiency statements.

C2.justification: The original captioner and hyperparameter limitations are largely retained in Appendix A. v2 adds explanations connecting failures to repetitive scenes and imperfect captions, hypothesizes that captioner pretraining explains weaker egocentric performance, and discusses hallucination and inspectability. It also acknowledges performance gaps to stronger proprietary models on Video-MME.

D1.justification: v2 discloses frame-sampling rates, relevance-count thresholds, Video-MME settings, and a detailed LifelongMemory reproduction procedure covering caption generation and output-processing fixes. It newly states that code is included in supplementary material, although that availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Hardware and prompts remain; some explicit IntentQA captioner and hyperparameter details from v1 are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds references covering Video-MME, LVNet, Mistral/Mixtral, newer multimodal models, and hallucination research, while removing several older background references. Positioning increasingly emphasizes training-free comparisons, matched captioner/reasoner settings, and competition with video-trained models. The detailed CREMA discussion is removed, although its citation remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. The introduction reorganizes three challenges into two and replaces the contribution bullets with prose. IntentQA and limitations move to appendices, the analysis sections are reorganized, and ethics and reproducibility statements are added.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, Figure 2 is revised, and Figure 3 gains a logarithmic caption-count axis and VideoAgent curve. Benchmark tables are reorganized and distributed across the paper, several new analytical tables appear, and the error-bar table disappears. Figure 6 adds a failure visualization; the existing successful examples remain. Typography and page layout also change throughout.

improvement.justification: v2 better supports long-duration applicability and efficiency through hour-scale video evaluation, direct timing measurements, matched open-source comparisons, and failure analysis. The net gain is limited by removing uncertainty reporting and leaving reporting inconsistencies. In particular, NExT-QA is called both validation and test, and the claim of lower runtime than both LLoVi variants conflicts with Table 3: VideoTree-best takes 20.1 seconds versus 3.9 for LLoVi-fast.
